intro: Professionals and everyday users convert cubic feet (ft³) to gallons (us) (gal (US)) when working across imperial and us_customary standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One cubic foot equals 7.480519 gallons (us), while 1 gallon (us liquid) equals 0.133681 cubic feet. Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many gallons (us) (gal (US)) are in 1 cubic foot (ft³)?
faqs.answer: There are 7.48051948 gallons (us) (gal (US)) in 1 cubic foot (ft³), which rounds to 7.4805 gal (US) for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 gallon (us liquid) equals 0.133681 cubic feet.

faqs.question: How do I convert cubic feet to gallons (us) (ft³ to gal (US))?
faqs.answer: To convert cubic feet to gallons (us), use the formula: gal (US) = ft³ × 7.48051948. For example, converting 10 ft³ gives 74.8052 gal (US).

faqs.question: What is 10 cubic feet in gallons (us)?
faqs.answer: 10 cubic feet (ft³) equals exactly 74.8052 gallons (us) (gal (US)) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
